sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, Chapter Seven continued, floods and storms, winter driving, being stranded, skidding, anti-lock brakes and reduced visibility

The audience is first-time, never-licensed Vermont applicants, typically teenagers on the learner's permit and junior license path and adults applying for a first driver's license, reading at a plain-English level with no assumed driving vocabulary. This section teaches what to do in storms and floods, how to prepare a vehicle and a trip for winter, how to survive a stranding, why skids happen and how to recover, how anti-lock brakes change braking, and when headlights and which beams are required. The content assumes no prior rule knowledge and no prerequisites beyond literacy; every term the section introduces is defined in the glossary lines of part C.

corpus_stability.reason: The Vermont Driver's Manual is a single pinned edition (Vermont Driver’s Manual 2025; VN-007 07/2024 MTC) revised no more than once a year by the issuer; no faster-changing corpus feeds this section.
